outcomeNote: restricted to a case where the mitzva is not absolute

segments.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן מִשּׁוּם רְשׁוּת: לֹא דָּנִין. וְהָא מִצְוָה קָעָבֵיד! לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִיכָּא דַּעֲדִיף מִינֵּיהּ.
segments.en: § It was taught in the mishna: «And the following» are acts that are prohibited on Shabbat and are notable «because they are optional,» i.e., which involve an aspect of a mitzva but are not complete mitzvot: «One may not judge.» The Gemara asks: «But doesn’t one perform» a full-fledged «mitzva» by acting as a judge in a court? Why is it categorized as optional rather than as a full-fledged mitzva? The Gemara answers: «No,» it is «necessary» for the mishna to categorize it as optional, as it is speaking of a case «where there is» another person «who is more» qualified «than he.» Since the other person can judge even better, it is not considered an absolute mitzva for the first one to judge.
